title: Series and parallel circuits sheet
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 58 (Series and parallel circuits sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 58: Series and parallel circuits. To understand how current and voltage behave in series and parallel circuits

model.title: A 12 V supply is connected to a 4 Ω and an 8 Ω resistor in series. Find the current and the voltage across each resistor.
A 6.0 V supply is connected to a 12 Ω and a 6.0 Ω resistor in parallel. Find the current in each branch and the total current.
A current of 2.5 A flows through a lamp for 40 s. Calculate the charge that flows.

questions.q: Two lamps in parallel on 6 V. Currents 0.4 A and 0.6 A. Supply current? Voltage across each? [2 marks]
questions.model: Parallel: currents in branches add: 0.4 + 0.6 = 1.0 A. Voltage across each branch equals the supply: 6 V.

questions.q: In series, the supply is 9 V and one lamp has 4 V. The other?
In series, the current is 0.3 A at one point. Elsewhere?
Core: Six circuit diagrams (portal worksheet): find the missing currents and voltages.
questions.a: Answers in the key, e.g. junction: 1.5 A in, 0.5 A in one branch, 1.0 A in the other.
questions.model: Teacher solves diagram 1: series with 12 V supply and 3 V across lamp A: lamp B has 9 V; same current everywhere.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why homes use parallel circuits for lighting. [3 marks]
questions.a: Each lamp gets the full supply voltage (1); each can be switched independently (1); if one fails the others still work (1).

questions.q: Stretch: Three identical lamps in parallel on 12 V draw 1.5 A in total. Current in each, and resistance of each?
In parallel, the voltage across each branch...
Big question: why do the other lights stay on when one bulb blows?
questions.a: Household lighting is in parallel: each lamp is on its own branch.
